answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: A mine operator must immediately contact MSHA, without delay and within 15 minutes, after an accident that causes a death of an individual at the mine.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately, without delay and within 15 minutes, once it knows or should know an accident has occurred.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the accidents requiring this immediate notification.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where rock dust is required and no methane is present in the ventilating current, the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust in all underground areas of a coal mine must be maintained at not less than 80 percent incombustible content.

claims.text: The combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be maintained so that incombustible content is not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: it shall be distributed upon the top, floor, and sides of all underground areas of a coal mine and maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: This 80 percent requirement increases only when methane is present, implying 80 percent is the baseline minimum where no methane is present.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: Under 30 CFR 75.1714, the self-rescue device made available to each underground coal miner must be approved and adequate to protect that person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect that person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: At an underground metal or nonmetal mine, evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills shall be held at least once every six months to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training before such miner is assigned to work duties, with training conducted to duplicate actual underground conditions and about 8 hours given at the minesite.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties. Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: Based on the provided regulatory text, MSHA's noise standard requires that a miner's noise exposure be measured as a time-weighted average over the full work shift (an 8-hour TWA, referred to as "TWA8"), and this TWA8 is calculated using a 90-decibel criterion level together with a 5-decibel exchange rate (with A-weighting and slow response settings), without any adjustment for hearing protectors. The mine operator must ensure that no miner's noise exposure during any work shift exceeds this permissible exposure level, and under no circumstances may a miner be exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA (unadjusted for hearing protection). The specific numeric decibel value of the "permissible exposure level" itself (as distinct from the criterion level used in the dose formula) is not explicitly stated in these excerpts.

claims.text: The mine operator must ensure no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise exceeding the permissible exposure level.
claims.quote: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise that exceeds the permissible exposure level.

claims.text: A miner's noise dose determination must use a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate.
claims.quote: Use a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate; and

claims.text: The dose determination reflects the miner's full work shift, and the operator uses Table 62-2 to convert dose readings to equivalent TWA8 readings.
claims.quote: The mine operator must use Table 62-2 when converting from dose readings to equivalent TWA8 readings.

claims.text: No miner may be exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA, measured without adjustment for hearing protectors.
claims.quote: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA, as determined without adjustment for the use of any hearing protector.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines, berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway. This requirement applies to both surface (30 CFR 56.9300) and underground (30 CFR 57.9300) metal and nonmetal mines.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway (surface mines, 56.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway (underground mines, 57.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air in an approved refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: Mechanisms and procedures must be provided so that, within the refuge alternative, the breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

claims.text: The ERP must specify sufficient food and water to sustain the maximum number of persons for at least 96 hours (or 48 hours if advance arrangements are made).
claims.quote: A minimum of 2,000 calories of food and 2.25 quarts of potable water per person per day in approved containers sufficient to sustain the maximum number of persons reasonably expected to use the refuge alternative for at least 96 hours, or for 48 hours if advance arrangements are made under paragraph (c) of this section;

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided reference materials do not contain any information about OSHA's construction trenching standards or the depth at which a protective system such as shoring or a trench box is required. The chunks available only cover mining-related regulations (30 CFR Parts 56, 57, and 77) concerning slope/shaft safety plans, hoisting buckets, and roll-over protective structures (ROPS) for mining equipment — none of which address OSHA trench safety requirements.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about FAA certification requirements for drone pilots at mine sites. The chunks only cover MSHA regulations on site-specific hazard awareness training, surface facilities waivers, seal installation, and mine map certification—none of which address drone operations or FAA pilot certification.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not address EPA stormwater discharge permits. They only cover unrelated topics—MSHA permits for experimental electric face equipment in gassy mines/tunnels (30 CFR 18.82) and Coal Mine Safety District Manager permits for mining operations near bodies of water (30 CFR 75.1716-2 and 75.1716-3). None of them discuss EPA stormwater permitting requirements for mine site runoff.
